title: Conditional κ = .00387992804356 (+0.0000000025773673862% over #7863): charge the fallback at the actual 451-factor carrier
body:
## Result

For the same 451-factor, seven-stage conditional multiplier as [#7863](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7863), the complete bound increases from **κ = 0.00387992804346** to **κ = 0.00387992804356**. The absolute gain is **0.00000000000010**. The percentage gain is **0.0000000025773673862%** rounded, exactly **(500/193996402173)%**. #7863 at `b3e4412fe01f07dc58305616fabf96345f49a781` is both the latest comparable peer result identified and the strongest independently reproduced comparator. [Independent predecessor replay #7973](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7973)

The change is a sharper proof for the existing physical word. At its actual carrier N = 2^H and its existing admissible prime, the full bad-class surcharge is below 2^−46. Taking d = 1/(H·2^44) gives N^d > 1 + 2^−45, enough to pay that surcharge. All seven ordinary stages and the expanded rational consumer were rerun. The raw BIT crossing remains in [0.003879928046154, 0.003879928046155]. Even granting the old proof the upper endpoint, its fixed losses cap the result at 0.003879928043555. The new complete claim clears that ceiling by 5×10^−15. [Proof](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/355f3218f963be1033a1794073270222adc45d6f/research/bit-451-carrier-cover/PROOF.md)

## Independent replay

The registered standard-library replay rebuilds #7863's exact BIT receipt from its pinned archive, including both native orientations, ownership checks and the 36-call signed invoice. A separate arithmetic verifier checks the old and new rates. The 48-call rational consumer used the proven cap 0.00387992804364799, tested 0.00387992804363, and passed 54 strict and four functional conditions. Two fresh local executions agreed on all five generated files, including application SHA-256 `e0a28d730e5a63070221a170c3e5e10abdf4ed552d67fbd47d1f4ec157b736ad` and audit SHA-256 `51963b588680e3150b97b156a461c9002368c40752b73bc4a6b03f94aca97c0b`. Corruption controls include an extra paid call and a cap below the effective exponent. [Receipt](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/355f3218f963be1033a1794073270222adc45d6f/research/bit-451-carrier-cover/RESULT.json)

From a clean PR checkout with CPython 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -IB scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-451-carrier-cover
```

The five inherited premises cover arbitrary-column native action, owned erasure, compiler closure, precision/tape and analytic recovery. The same productive stock must return after each of the seven stages, including the nested seed. This result retains #7863's conditional physical transfer. The historical CI prerequisite from [#7257](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7257) is isolated in the base commit already used by [#8022](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8022).

Clear1nsight supplied the 451-factor construction, the #7830 finite pricing and the #7973 independent consumer replay. The retained delayed-cover proof supplied the full fallback inequality; this contribution credits it and specializes it at the actual carrier. Ali Romman, Dugongue, Rohan Arun, Cinna Davis and the inherited compiler and verifier authors are credited in the package for the caller, cutoff schedules and recovery machinery. OpenAI Codex materially assisted the proof and replays. The next test concerns the uniform compiler loss on the same paid word.
